caption:
Flood season and pipeline theft season overlap in the Niger Delta, and that overlap is not a coincidence. Rising creek levels reduce foot and boat patrol frequency along exposed reaches. Illegal tie-in points are easier to conceal under higher water and thicker vegetation growth that the rains bring. Product moves faster through flooded waterways that double as transport routes for the stolen volume.

None of this is new. It is public record in incident reporting from the region, and it is the reason theft reports historically climb alongside rainfall totals rather than against them.

Dam releases add a second variable. Reservoir operators schedule discharge for power generation and irrigation demand, not for theft-season risk downstream. A release timed for a generation target can raise water levels in exactly the reaches where reduced visibility already favors tapping. Two decisions made for two different reasons compound into one window of elevated risk for the same communities.

Understanding the seasonal mechanism matters for where attention gets allocated, independent of what any single system detects.

Two operating decisions, two different purposes, one overlapping window of risk for the same downstream communities.
Worth knowing where to look before the rains peak, not after. #NigerDelta #FloodSeason

card.headline: Flood season is also theft season
